1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night

The rain had been falling on Doldari for three days straight. Kim Haneul's older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and ever since, Haneul had been running the village's little pharmacy on her own.
When dusk came she closed the shutters, counted the day's takings, put out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when a frantic knocking came from the door downstairs, and then a man's voice. "Is anyone there?"
A young man stood at the door, soaked to the bone. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was soaked with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
"Please treat my wound," Park Junho said in a low voice. "I'll pay you. Would three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?"
He drew a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his coat. "This letter has to reach Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May."
Haneul thought to herself: the pharmacy was doing well, and the neighbours were already sick with envy — and now a stranger turns up in the middle of the night.
Even so, Haneul took no money and said only, "I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning."
2: As soon as day broke, the two of them set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back, and inside it were rice balls, herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain they met an old man, Lee Youngsoo, splitting firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice. The evening before, three strangers had been at the edge of the village, asking after a wounded young man.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each step firmly. Park Junho followed without a word.

At noon the rain stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted, and far off the roof of Cheongpungsa began to show. A nun stood at the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, the nun who welcomed guests at the temple.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal, and nodded. "The abbot has waited two years for this letter."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You saved my life." Haneul answered with a smile, "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the pharmacy." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
Toward evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit the oil lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
